input.title: Amara Okafor — UCL Particle Physics PhD Statement of Purpose
input.body:
I seek doctoral research in particle physics focused on detector reconstruction, uncertainty estimation, and computational methods. My academic preparation includes a Bachelor of Science in Physics from the University of Lagos, with relevant coursework in Quantum Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Statistical Mechanics, Mathematical Methods, Nuclear and Particle Physics, and Computational Physics.

My undergraduate research included a Monte Carlo study of muon-background rejection in a compact scintillator detector. This work developed my interest in connecting physical modelling with practical detector performance and computational analysis.

Since October 2024, I have worked as a research assistant at CERN OpenLab on uncertainty calibration for charged-particle track reconstruction. I use Python, C++, ROOT, and Geant4. I am also a co-author of “Fast uncertainty calibration for sparse detector tracks,” submitted to Computing and Software for Big Science in February 2026.

I want to deepen this work through doctoral research on robust reconstruction and uncertainty-aware computational techniques for particle-physics detectors. My longer-term aim is to contribute to research that improves the reliability and interpretability of measurements made with complex detector systems.

I am applying for full tuition support and a living stipend. I have never received a formal disciplinary finding.
